requests.discriminates: Roots z then a, where z imports b and b imports c, and every file has one parse error. The loader's single-threaded work group (fileloader.go:169, filesparser.go:264-278) is handed the two roots and must also run the tasks that parsing z and then b queue from inside a running task; a group that drains only what was queued before RunAndWait, or that drops or repeats a task, loses c or b from the file list or duplicates a diagnostic. GetSyntacticDiagnostics then collects all four files through a second single-threaded group (program.go:659) and sorts by file name. The file list records the load order and the diagnostics record that every task ran exactly once; the LIFO order of pop is not observable, because the parallel twin must give the same bytes.
requests.subject: syntacticDiagnostics

requests.discriminates: The same program built with single_threaded false, so the pinned loader uses core.NewWorkGroup(false): parallelWorkGroup.Queue starts every parse task on its own goroutine, including the ones queued from inside the running z and b tasks, and RunAndWait returns only when all of them are done. Its observation must equal the single-threaded twin byte for byte and the Rust sequential loader must match both, which makes the scheduling independence of the program result evidence rather than an assumption. A Queue that ran only the root tasks, or a RunAndWait that returned before the nested tasks finished, loses b or c.
